Bot-side formatting: HTML beats markdown for pipelines
Content · September 26, 2026 · 4 min read · Fast Scheduler team
Telegram’s text engine supports more formatting than any mainstream social platform — and half of it is hidden behind menus you’ve never opened. The full map, plus where formatting silently breaks.
Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough
— the basics; mobile composer hides underline behind the biu menu, desktop uses Ctrl+U.
Monospace
fixed-width
for dates, prices, code. Instantly signals “this is data”.
Spoilers
— tap-to-reveal black bars. Use as a curiosity device: predictions, answers, punchlines.
Block quotes
— the expandable quote block (desktop composer, and bots via the API). Underused and beautiful for citations.
Nested lists?
— no. Telegram has no native lists; people fake them with emoji bullets. That’s why “1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣” headers look native here.
In the message field:
`monospace`
work in most clients (and in the bots that accept markdown). Faster than any menu once it’s in your fingers.
Channels can use
custom emoji packs

— Telegram Premium users create them, but everyone sees them in your posts. A branded pack (your mascot reacting, your niche’s in-jokes) is a subtle status marker; packs are made in the @stickers bot. Custom emoji count against your formatting, not your character budget.
Copy-pasting from Word/Google Docs brings invisible characters that break formatting — paste into a plain editor first when it matters.
Editing a published post on a different device can drop entities the second client doesn’t render.
The native scheduler preserves formatting but shows no preview; scheduling bots compete on this — ControllerBot and
both render a preview of the final message before it queues, which catches broken markdown before your subscribers do.
One bolded takeaway per paragraph (the scanning layer).
One emoji per section header, never mid-sentence.
Monospace for anything a reader might copy: dates, prices, links.
Spoilers for genuine reveals — never for load-bearing information.
The composer's B/I menu is a subset. The full entity set includes:
(desktop: Ctrl+U),
monospace
via triple backticks with syntax highlighting for code,
spoilers
(hidden-until-tap text — perfect for solutions, leaks and price reveals),
hidden links
on arbitrary words,
block quotes
with nesting in newer clients, and the quietly powerful
expandable quote

: a collapsed "show more" block. Expandable quotes are the digest channel's best formatting weapon — twelve links, each summarized in a one-line quoted block, stays scannable instead of becoming a wall. None of these need a bot; most need the desktop app to discover.

Formatting survives differently depending on the path it takes. Forwards preserve everything. Copy-paste from desktop usually preserves entities but strips them from media captions. RSS-imported posts can lose nested quotes and custom emoji. Some third-party Android clients render custom emoji as their fallback packs. And previews outside Telegram — link cards on Twitter/X or Discord — show plain text only, which is why the first line of every post must work naked. The professional habit: keep one "torture test" message containing every entity, post it to a private test channel, forward it through every pipeline you use, and look at what arrives. Ten minutes of setup answers a year of "why did that post look broken?"

When content flows through bots — schedulers, RSS bridges, cross-posters — the parse mode decides fidelity. Telegram's markdown mode breaks on unescaped underscores in URLs and on stray asterisks; HTML mode (
<code>
<a href>
) is deterministic and copies cleanly between tools. The working rule: author by hand in the composer, but store
templates
in HTML inside your scheduler —

accepts formatted drafts, and most bots expose a preview command — so automated posts never surprise you with literal asterisks published to four thousand people. Whichever mode you standardize on, standardize: mixed-format pipelines are where formatting goes to die.
Common questions
How do I underline text in Telegram?
Mobile: select text → BIU menu → underline. Desktop: Ctrl+U (Cmd+U). Bots and scheduling tools accept underline entities too — it survives scheduling if the bot supports rich formatting.
What are Telegram spoilers?
Tap-to-reveal regions (||double pipes|| in markdown-style input). Great for answers and reveals; annoying if overused for basic information.
What is monospace used for in Telegram posts?
Anything data-like: dates, prices, commands, code. Fixed-width makes it visually distinct and copy-paste safe.
Does scheduling a post keep its formatting?
Yes with bots that support rich entities — ControllerBot and
preview and preserve bold, spoilers, monospace and custom emoji through editing and scheduling.
